summary.title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: Rethinking Retrieval for Agentic Search via Direct Corpus Interaction

details: Conventional lexical/dense retrievers expose a corpus only through a fixed similarity interface returning a top-k slice, so evidence discarded early cannot be recovered by stronger downstream reasoning; this bottlenecks agentic search that needs exact lexical constraints, weak-clue conjunctions, local context checks, and multi-step hypothesis revision.

Direct Corpus Interaction (DCI): a retrieval paradigm in which the agent searches the raw corpus directly with general-purpose terminal primitives (grep/rg, find/glob, file reads, bash pipelines, small scripts), with no embedding model, vector index, or retrieval API, so semantic interpretation moves from the index down into the agent.

Conceptual claim of 'retrieval interface resolution': the agent's power comes from being able to act on units finer than whole documents/passages, composing lexical filters and verifying exact spans in local context.
DCI-Agent-Lite: minimal Pi-based harness exposing only bash and read, backbone GPT-5.4 nano (high reasoning effort), max 300 turns; no retrieval-specific module.
DCI-Agent-CC: Claude Code as off-the-shelf CLI agent with Claude Sonnet 4.6 (medium effort), with web-search, web-fetch, and subagents disabled and the answer data directory blocked.

Runtime context-management layer with three mechanisms (tool-result truncation, zero-LLM compaction of older tool turns, model-generated summarization), instantiated as policies L0-L4 (e.g., L3 = 20k-char cap + compaction past 240k chars keeping last 12 turns).
Agentic search: BrowseComp-Plus over its official 100K-document corpus (avg ~5.2K words/doc), with a released BM25/Qwen3-Embedding-8B FAISS index used only for retrieval baselines.

Knowledge-intensive QA: NQ, TriviaQA, Bamboogle, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue over the 21M-passage 2018 Wikipedia dump (E5 index for retrieval baselines); 50 sampled examples per dataset except full Bamboogle.
IR ranking: BRIGHT (Biology, Earth Science, Economics, Robotics; full test sets) and BEIR (ArguAna, SciFact; 50 sampled queries each).
Retrieval agents on BrowseComp-Plus: official pipeline with BM25 or Qwen3-Embedding-8B paired with GPT-5, o3, GLM-4.7, Kimi K2, Claude Sonnet 4.5/4.6.
QA: R1-Searcher-7B, Search-R1-32B, ZeroSearch-7B, Verl-Tool-Search-7B-DAPO, ASearcher-Local-14B.
IR: BM25, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, GTE-Qwen2-7B-Instruct, plus reasoning rerankers Rank-R1-14B, Rank1-32B, ReasonRank-32B.
Answer accuracy judged by GPT-4.1 against short reference answers; NDCG@10 for IR ranking; API cost, latency, and tool-call counts reported.

New trajectory-level metrics: coverage (any / mean / all gold documents surfaced) and localization, a log-normalized segment-level score rewarding small exposed spans relative to full gold-document length, with an interface-specific mapping from tool outputs to snippets (path-only surfacing scored as a full-document snippet).
Tool-set expressivity: read+grep only vs full bash command set (100 BrowseComp-Plus samples).
Context-management policies L0-L4 on 100 sampled BrowseComp-Plus questions.
Corpus scaling: BrowseComp-Plus expanded from 100K to 200K and 400K documents by injecting FineWeb distractors.

key_findings.finding: Swapping a strong dense retriever for direct corpus interaction improves end-to-end agentic search accuracy while lowering cost.
key_findings.evidence: On BrowseComp-Plus with the same Claude Sonnet 4.6 backbone, replacing the Qwen3-Embedding-8B retrieval tool with DCI raises accuracy from 69.0% to 80.0% and cuts cost from $1,440 to $1,016 (-29.4%); DCI-Agent-CC also beats the best retrieval agent overall (GPT-5 + Qwen3-Embedding-8B, 71.7%) by 8.3 points, and DCI-Agent-Lite on GPT-5.4 nano reaches 62.9% for only $93 versus 66.0% at $740 for o3 + Qwen3-Embedding-8B.

key_findings.finding: DCI's advantage comes from higher-resolution use of already-surfaced evidence rather than surfacing more gold documents.
key_findings.evidence: With matched Sonnet 4.6 backbones, DCI-Agent-CC wins 176 BrowseComp-Plus questions the retrieval agent misses versus 76 the reverse; in 142 of those 176 the retrieval agent had already surfaced at least one gold document (83 partial-chain, 59 full-recall post-retrieval failures). DCI-Agent-Lite has much lower mean gold coverage than Qwen3-Embedding-8B (28.0 vs 56.7) and comparable coverage-any (70.0 vs 74.0) but far higher localization (48.4 vs 21.7), alongside a +28-point accuracy gain.

key_findings.finding: Index-free terminal search is also competitive as a general retrieval method for multi-hop QA and reasoning-intensive ranking.
key_findings.evidence: DCI-Agent-CC reaches 83.0 average accuracy on the six knowledge-intensive QA datasets versus 52.3 for the strongest baseline ASearcher-Local-14B (+30 on HotpotQA, +26 on 2Wiki, +50 on MuSiQue), and 68.5 average NDCG@10 on BRIGHT/BEIR versus 47.0 for ReasonRank-32B; DCI-Agent-Lite is second overall in both suites (68.0 accuracy; 56.7 NDCG@10).

key_findings.finding: Most of the benefit needs only minimal tooling; a full shell adds incremental gains at markedly higher cost.
key_findings.evidence: Restricted to read+grep, DCI-Agent-Lite achieves 61% on 100 BrowseComp-Plus samples versus 45% for the Qwen3-Embedding-8B retrieval agent at nearly identical tool-call intensity; enabling bash adds a further 12 points but substantially increases tool usage, latency, and compute. Bash usage is dominated by compositional search (rg | head 56.2%, rg | rg 20.6%) with full-document cat reads at 0.1%.

key_findings.finding: DCI has a clear operating envelope: it scales in search depth but degrades sharply with corpus breadth, and context management shows a non-monotonic sweet spot.
key_findings.evidence: Expanding BrowseComp-Plus from 100K to 200K docs raises DCI-Agent-CC tool calls per question from 38.5 to 86.9, more than doubles latency and cost, and drops accuracy 13.6 points; at 400K accuracy falls to 37.5% with 122.4 calls and 20 budget-exhausted examples. Across context policies, L3 gives the best accuracy (77) despite lower retained gold coverage than L1 (27.0 vs 31.3), while L2 is worst (69) and L4 declines after the L3 peak.
